transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording enabled)
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenny (Redwood SE), Maya (Glasswater - Head of ML), Raj (Glasswater - Infra), Hannah (Glasswater - CTO)

Summary:
Quick discovery for Glasswater's plan to move some heavy inference into dedicated reserved GPUs. Primary concerns: tenant isolation (they run multi-tenant models), burst handling for unpredictable traffic, cost vs latency tradeoffs, and on-prem/VPC security requirements. Agreed to run a perf PoC and exchange security docs.

Topics covered:
- Reserved GPU pool sizing and topology options (node fencing, per-tenant pools, shared hotpool)
- Burst strategy: prewarm, hot pools, burst to hosted fallback, pricing for burst vs committed
- Isolation: VPC/private deployment vs dedicated in Redwood Dedicated, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration
- Performance expectations: tokens/sec, p99 latency targets, KV cache and cold-start behavior
- Compliance: SOC 2, data residency, SSO/SAML integration and contract timelines

Action items (recap): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:08] Maya: Hi, Maya here, head of ML at Glasswater. We're evaluating options for inference, mainly looking at reserving capacity for some critical workloads.
[00:13] Raj: Raj, infra lead, I'll be the one doing the PoC with you folks.
[00:16] Hannah: Hannah, CTO, just listening in for architecture implications.
[00:20] Jenny: Jenny Huang, solutions engineer at Redwood — I'll lead the technical side.
[00:24] Samir: Great. The goal today is to understand your workloads, isolation needs, burst profile, and timeline so we can propose reserved GPU configs and a plan. Maya, can you walk us through the ML use cases?
[00:35] Maya: Sure. We run two main inference patterns. One is a low-latency chat assistant for enterprise customers — that's sensitive to p99 latency, want under 350ms if possible. The other is a batch reranker and some long-context summarization jobs that are more throughput-oriented. Both need some level of tenant data separation, especially the assistant.
[00:52] Jenny: When you say tenant separation, do you need physical isolation (i.e., dedicated nodes per tenant) or logical isolation with strong RBAC and encrypted volumes?
[01:00] Maya: For our top-tier customers we prefer physical isolation — they contractually insist on node-level tenancy. For the rest, logical isolation is OK. So we need a mix.
[01:11] Raj: To add, we also have unpredictable bursts — up to 3x our baseline during peak events. We want to avoid cold-start latency spikes.
[01:20] Samir: OK, that's common. Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools and we can do a hybrid: dedicated nodes pinned to specific tenants and a shared hot pool for overflow. We also have burst to hosted fallback if the dedicated pool saturates — that keeps requests alive while we scale.
[01:36] Hannah: Pricing question up front — how does burst to hosted get billed versus reserved capacity?
[01:42] Samir: Reserved is a steady monthly commit — your per-month reserved unit. Burst to hosted is billed as usage (per-token / per-inference) at a higher rate. We'll send concrete numbers, but the pattern is predictable: baseline commit covers X tokens and bursts are metered.
[01:57] Maya: We care about the QoE though. If a request fails over to hosted, will we see different model variants or quantization that change outputs?
[02:05] Jenny: Good point. We can arrange model pinning across variants — a compatible model variant on hosted for seamless fallback. There may be slight differences if quantized variants are used — we'll flag regressions in the evals.
[02:18] Raj: How about prewarming/hot pools — how long to prewarm a model and what's the warm pool sizing strategy?
[02:26] Jenny: Prewarm depends on model size and GPU type. For a 30B model on A100-ish hardware, cold->warm is roughly 30-90s to warm the KV cache depending on prompt lengths and batch patterns. Hot pools keep one or more instances with KV primed; you pay for the reserved node but it drastically cuts cold starts.
[02:44] Maya: So we'd reserve a small per-tenant node for tier-1, and a shared hot pool for the rest?
[02:48] Jenny: Exactly. Another knob is prefix caching — if your assistants share prefixes we can cache those and reduce warm time.
[02:55] Samir: Let's talk numbers — Raj, can you ballpark token/sec and typical seq length?
[03:01] Raj: Baseline is ~400 QPS across all tenants; peak bursts push to 1200 QPS for 5-30 minutes. Typical prompt is 350-600 tokens, responses 80-150 tokens.
[03:14] Jenny: Good, that helps. We'll propose a pool to hit your p99 target and a hot pool sized for burst smoothing. Also discussing continuous batching; it increases throughput but can add a few ms latency — tradeoff you can tune.
[03:29] Maya: On security: we require SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS-managed keys for customer data at rest. Are those supported with private deployments?
[03:38] Jenny: Yes. Private deployments + Redwood Dedicated can integrate with your KMS/HSM and SAML SSO. Audit logs are shipped to your SIEM; we can illustrate log formats. We'll attach the SOC2 package and our security checklist.
[03:52] Hannah: Does private mean we bring hardware? Or Redwood deploys in our VPC?
[03:56] Samir: Two options — Redwood Private (customer VPC with control plane isolated) or on-prem package where you host compute and we ship the control plane. Both support KMS/HSM and isolated networking. We'll map pros/cons in the doc.
[04:08] Raj: Network egress and data residency are critical — some tenants require EU-only data paths. Can we pin model serving regionally?
[04:15] Jenny: Yes, routing policies can pin traffic by customer region. Also we support per-route model version pinning and rollout policies.
[04:24] Maya: About observability — we need token-level cost, per-tenant latency percentiles, and traces to tie tokens to API keys.
[04:33] Samir: Redwood Console gives per-token breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We can create tenant-specific views with RBAC.
[04:40] Raj: For the PoC, we want to run 3 traces: normal, burst, and a high-concurrency rerank batch. What metrics should we capture?
[04:48] Jenny: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, KV cache hit rates, batch size distribution, and quality deltas on a sample prompt set. We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet template.
[05:02] Maya: If we see output regressions when using quantized models to reduce cost, can Redwood provide a rollback/fallback policy?
[05:09] Jenny: Yes — automatic fallback to higher-precision variant on quality regression triggers. We also recommend canary rollouts and automatic rollback rules.
[05:18] Samir: Let's discuss timeline. When would you like the PoC?
[05:21] Maya: Ideally weeks, not months — we want pilot in 2-3 weeks, full production in a quarter if PoC is good.
[05:27] Raj: We can prep infra quickly if we get a checklist.
[05:30] Jenny: We'll send a private deployment checklist and a minimal PoC plan: model artifacts, keys, sample traffic, and test harness.
[05:37] Samir: About contract terms — typical reserved commitments run 3, 12, or 24-month. We can model expected unit economics for each.
[05:45] Hannah: Are there penalties for bursting above reserved?
[05:48] Samir: Bursts are billed as metered usage; no penalty other than higher unit price, except for dedicated burst queue delays if capacity is limited. We'll share example math.
[05:58] Maya: One concern — our rerank jobs can be GPU-memory heavy. Do you support various GPU types and quantization strategies?
[06:04] Jenny: Yes, we can recommend quantization (4-bit/8-bit) based on your model and accuracy constraints. For memory-heavy reranks we might prefer larger GPU types or sharded execution. We'll include suggested configs.
[06:16] Raj: On the network side, what are the prewarming costs? We want to know steady-state cost of keeping a hot pool of N instances.
[06:23] Samir: We'll produce a cost example: cost = reserved node monthly price + marginal prewarm cost; hot pool sizing has diminishing returns beyond a certain number.
[06:33] Maya: Ok. If we do Dedicated in our VPC, who manages upgrades/patches?
[06:38] Jenny: With Redwood Private in a customer's VPC, we can offer managed ops or hand it to your infra team. Patching can be scheduled; for on-prem you typically run ops with Redwood support.
[06:49] Raj: For auditing we need immutable logs for model invocations. Can logs be shipped off-box?
[06:53] Jenny: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded to your ELK/Splunk/Datadog endpoint with retention controls.
[06:59] Maya: Any gotchas we should know about before committing?
[07:02] Jenny: Main ones: model variant mismatch during fallback (we mitigate with evals), cold-start tail latency for large models (use prewarm/hot pools), and network egress for cross-region fallbacks.
[07:15] Samir: We'll include a recommended topology: per-tenant dedicated nodes for top-tier customers, a shared hot pool, and a hosted fallback route. Also a suggested commit level and burst buffer size.
[07:26] Hannah: For procurement, we may need security attestation docs and a draft MSA. Can you send those?
[07:30] Samir: Yes — we'll send SOC2 pack, sample MSA, data processing addendum, and pricing.
[07:36] Maya: Cool. Quick clarifying Q: are there any limits on simultaneous model variants per pool?
[07:42] Jenny: Only practical limits — more variants increase memory pressure; we recommend pinning a small set per pool.
[07:49] Raj: One last infra detail — will KV cache survive node failover or do we have cache warming penalties after preemption?
[07:56] Jenny: KV cache is in-GPU memory (per-instance). On failover you get cold states until cache warms — that's why prewarming or sticky routing matters. We also have techniques to persist some caches to faster NVMe based on use case, but it adds complexity.
[08:12] Samir: Ok we're at the point of next steps — Samir to send pricing, Jenny to send security docs and PoC plan, Raj/Maya to provide traffic traces and prompt sets.
[08:23] Maya: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[08:26] Hannah: No, thanks.
[08:28] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up over email with the attachments and schedule the PoC.
[51:30] (call ends, recording stops)
